item.title: No need to take blood pressure pills now? Scientists are testing a device that can reduce BP by stimulating nerves
item.description: A recent study shows that stimulating the ear can help lower blood pressure. Known as transcutaneous autonomic neuromodulation, this innovative approach may offer an effective solution for managing hypertension. In a clinical trial with 63 participants who struggled with uncontrolled hypertension despite medication, those with severe cases displayed encouraging results. However, further research is essential to validate the efficacy of this non-invasive technique. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In the 1940s, Ohio built a 200-foot dam for a village; now, it’s restoring a 14-mile creek
item.description: Ohio's Cloverlick Dam, built in the 1940s, is being removed to restore the natural flow of Cloverlick Creek. This restoration project aims to improve water quality and reconnect aquatic habitats that have been disrupted for decades. Removal of the dam is expected to create a safer environment for recreational activities like fishing and kayaking. Funding for the project is being provided by the H2Ohio Rivers Program and federal grants. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Natalie Portman's €15.2 million Paris mansion near the Eiffel Tower has a 100-year-old history
item.description: Natalie Portman purchased a 550-square-metre mansion in Paris for €15.2 million in September 2023. Built in 1912, the four-storey property once served as an embassy before undergoing extensive renovation. Located near the Eiffel Tower, the residence features a garden, gym, library, wine cellar and a glass-roofed reception room. The actress bought the property months before her divorce from Benjamin Millepied was finalised. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How ancient Chinese night watchmen patrolled streets, used ‘dripping buckets’ to tell time
item.description: In ancient China, before the advent of mechanical clocks and digital devices, people relied mainly on night watchmen to keep time, prevent fires and maintain their daily routines. But how did the watchmen tell the time? Chinese night watchmen mainly used two methods: clepsydras and incense sticks. A clepsydra, also known as a water clock, measures time through the regulated flow of water from a vessel. The ancient Chinese divided the night into five gengs. Each geng lasted around two hours,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: More than 400.000 protest across France
item.description: Saturday’s demonstrations across France were largely peaceful, easing fears of a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. Hundreds of thousands took to the streets to demand action on the rising cost of living and more funding for public services, with students, workers and retirees marching side by side. Many say their anger shows no sign of fading. The government put turnout at 410,000 nationwide, while the CGT union estimated the figure was almost twice as high. Here’s Jack Pownall with more. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France to protest against government
item.description: Hundreds of thousands marched across France on Saturday protesting the rising cost of living and a lack of government resources for essential services like schools. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully they ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrested across the country. France 24 International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry shares further details. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: Pakistan reopens Iran border crossing after week-long suspension of trade
item.description: Following a week-long closure due to security threats, Pakistan has reopened the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing with Iran. This pivotal reopening facilitates the flow of commercial goods that had been halted, leading to concerns regarding the availability of LPG and rising food and energy costs as winter neared. Enhanced security protocols are now in place to safeguard transport, bringing much-needed relief to local traders and transporters. Publicado también por: The Times of India - World. item.description: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. item.title: Ukraine drone attacks kill three, injure 14 in Russia’s Belgorod region
item.description: A drone strike carried out by Ukrainian forces hit Belgorod, leading to two confirmed deaths and injuring at least 13 people. Local officials highlighted significant destruction to housing, vehicles, and local infrastructure. Additionally, a nearby village reported another fatality and injuries stemming from the ongoing hostilities. These events underscore the ongoing violence escalating along the Russia-Ukraine border, and tensions continue to mount in the region. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Veteran Hong Kong stock commentator Louie Shum Chun-ying has died aged 66, with a police source revealing he had a history of heart disease and diabetes. item.description: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. item.description: A shooting occurred near a football stadium in Tallahassee during homecoming weekend at Florida A&M University. item.description: South Korean teenager Leo Park, 16, who began sharing his architectural sketches on Instagram in 2019, has collaborated with British company Colour Your Streets on a colouring book featuring 30 UK cities.
